questions.prompt: After a crash, the log holds an assistant message with a tool call but no tool result. What goes wrong if you only append turn/end and carry on?
options: Nothing; the model ignores calls from earlier turns
The provider rejects the next request because the call has no matching result
The tool runs again automatically on the next request
The JSONL file can no longer be loaded
questions.explanation: Derived history still contains the assistant message, and providers require every tool call to be answered by a result with the same id. The session cannot continue until each call has one.

questions.prompt: call_1 has a tool/call event in the log; call_2 does not. Which synthetic results should they get?
options: Both get 'never started', since neither has a result
Both get 'outcome unknown', to be safe
call_1 gets 'outcome unknown'; call_2 gets 'never started'
call_1 gets a success result; call_2 gets 'never started'
questions.explanation: A recorded tool/call means the tool started, so whether it finished is unknown. No tool/call means it never started, so running it again is safe.

questions.prompt: Why does the 'outcome unknown' result tell the model to run the tool again only if it is idempotent?
options: Repeating a tool that may already have acted, such as sending an email, could do it twice
Idempotent tools cannot fail, so repeating them always succeeds
The provider rejects repeated calls to tools that are not idempotent
Only idempotent tools produce a tool/call event
questions.explanation: An idempotent tool has the same effect whether it runs once or twice. A tool that may have already sent an email or charged a card should be checked first, not repeated blindly.

diagramRequest.title: A crash mid-step and the resume that repairs it
diagramRequest.show: The loop appends events 1-5 to the JSONL file, the process is killed after tool/call for call_1, and on restart resume reads the file, finds call_1 started and call_2 not started, appends two synthetic error results, step/end and turn/end interrupted, and the next request to the model is accepted.
